    Changelog

    Source: NEWS.md

    songR 1.0.0

    First stable release and first CRAN submission.

    Model lineage and feature contracts

    • Record projection revisions, parent lineage and explicit reprojection policy on incremental updates. Clarify update-batch outputs and frozen prediction.
    • Add an explicit optional update seed for reproducible retraining; the default continues to use the current random stream.
    • Bind named training features and optional declared measurement metadata to models; prediction and updates reject incompatible feature order or metadata. Unnamed and legacy models retain positional compatibility.

    Performance

    • Faster core training: the per-sample k-nearest-coding-vector search now reuses the distances already computed for the quantization step instead of recomputing them and copying the active codebook on every sample. Embeddings are unchanged (bit-identical).
    • predict() and the codebook-graph plotting paths (plot() / autoplot()) are vectorized.
    • Mapping point labels to coding vectors (codebook and graph plots) and the centroid step after dispersion group the points in a single pass instead of scanning all points once per coding vector.

    Printing

    • print() names the class in its header line (<song_model> SONG model), as the other packages of the suite do.

    Plots

    • plot() draws a legend at the plot corner or edge where it covers the fewest points, in one or two columns: the levels of a categorical color_by with at most 12 levels, or a key of five evenly spaced values for a numeric color_by. Use legend = FALSE to omit it.
    • plot() forwards graphical arguments such as main, xlab, ylab, pch and cex through ...; they override the defaults of the method. These previously failed as duplicated arguments.
    • plot() and autoplot() draw up to eight categories in the Okabe-Ito palette, which stays distinguishable under the common forms of color vision deficiency, instead of pastel hues (plot()) and the default ggplot2 hues (autoplot()). More than eight categories keep evenly spaced hues.
    • autoplot() draws a numeric color_by on the viridis scale and missing values in gray, as plot() does. Adding a color scale to the returned plot still replaces the scale; ggplot2 now reports the replacement with a message because the plot always carries a scale.
    • The edges of plot(type = "graph") and the eighth category color follow the foreground color of the graphics device (par("fg")), so they stay visible on a dark background, for example in the dark mode of the comparison app. On a white background the edges look as before.

    Comparison app

    • The app loads the Bootstrap styles that its layout relies on: the settings and the SONG, t-SNE and UMAP panels now sit side by side instead of below each other, and the inputs are styled as intended.
    • The comparison plots draw larger points and legend text, and in dark mode they leave out the dark end of the plasma scale, which was invisible on the dark panel.

    Bug fixes

    • Validate scalar, finite hyperparameters before native training. Fractional integer controls, non-positive update epochs/learning rates and damaged saved model dimensions now fail with an R error rather than being truncated or passed to C++.
    • Accept a single new observation in predict() and reject zero-column inputs.
    • Keep cumulative training counts finite when updates exceed R’s integer range.
    • Exclude native coverage instrumentation files from source archives.
    • Map codebook colors from the current update batch rather than cumulative training labels; handle prototypes with only missing labels. Correct the README to distinguish frozen projection from model retraining.
    • autoplot() no longer errors for type = "codebook" or type = "graph" when color_by has input-point length; like plot(), it now maps the labels to coding vectors.
    • The UMAP dispersion step now winsorizes the embedding before building the UMAP init, so a single drifted coding vector can no longer dominate the min-max scaling and strand its points as a far outlier. This removes occasional outliers and improves cluster separation (e.g. Fashion-MNIST reproduction AMI 0.50 -> 0.55). Only the dispersion = TRUE path is affected; the core SONG embedding is unchanged.
    • The UMAP dispersion now uses a stronger refinement (200 epochs, learning rate 1.0, min_dist = 0.1) instead of the reference’s very gentle 11-epoch step. songR’s raw embedding is more collapsed than the reference’s on hard, multi-class data, and the gentle step left it stranded near one axis; the stronger refinement makes the embedding use the full plane and, in benchmarks, improves AMI on every tested dataset (MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, COIL-20, Samusik, Wong). Only the dispersion = TRUE visualization changes; the core SONG embedding stays frozen.
    • The Shiny comparison app no longer claims SONG stops training early, and its documented k and epochs defaults match the implementation.
    • plot() maps a numeric color_by linearly onto the sequential viridis palette and treats logical vectors as categories. Numeric values used to be passed to the graphics device as color numbers, so negative values raised an error and values below 1 drew invisible points. As a consequence, whole-number labels supplied as numbers are now drawn on the sequential palette instead of the session palette; pass a factor for categorical colors. Missing labels are drawn in gray instead of being left out.
    • With dispersion = TRUE, coding vectors without assigned points are placed inside the refined layout (at the edge-weighted mean of their occupied graph neighbors, or at the occupied coding vector nearest in input space) instead of keeping raw SONG coordinates from a different coordinate system. Codebook and graph plots now share the scale of the embedding and predict() stays inside the layout. model$embedding is unchanged; model$Y and the model identifier change for models that contain such coding vectors.
    • Codebook and graph plots summarize numeric point values by their mean per coding vector and keep a continuous color scale. They used to reduce numeric values to the most frequent one and draw it as a category.
    • autoplot() reports a one-dimensional embedding with the same error as plot() instead of “subscript out of bounds”.
    • print() and summary() accept models saved before the converged field existed.
    • The comparison app no longer passes a reactive as the plot background, which raised a warning on every render.
    • The documentation of the comparison app (run_songR_app(), README and article) describes the implemented features. RDS upload, an incremental mode and export buttons were documented but are not part of the app; the article shows the equivalent code.

    Robustness

    • song() validates max_age and max_prototypes.
    • plot() and autoplot() reject a color_by that is a list or a data frame with an informative error instead of an internal sorting error.
    • song(verbose = TRUE) reports when the dispersion step is skipped because ‘uwot’ is not installed.
    • Diverging training, caused by a large learning rate alpha or by features on an extreme scale, is reported by song() and update() as an error of class song_error_diverged with advice, instead of the native message “sort_index(): detected NaN”. The error is raised when coding vectors become nonfinite or end more than 1000 times farther from zero than the data; such fits used to be returned as valid models. Values of alpha above 1 overshoot and can be unstable without triggering the error, and the documentation of alpha says so.
    • All user-facing messages now use cli, with errors signaled at the calling function for clearer tracebacks. Messages and behavior are otherwise unchanged.

    Documentation

    • song() documents every field of the model object, the effect of seed on the random number stream of the session, the memory needed for max_prototypes and how the dispersed layout is built. update() documents that it does not repeat the dispersion step.
    • The autoplot() example now draws a plot, and plot() shows continuous coloring and the codebook graph.
    • The README lists installation from GitHub and the CTTIR R-universe, its quick start runs as written, and the CRAN badges and the CRAN installation line are omitted until the package is on CRAN.
    • The vignettes describe updates as continued training in which prototypes may move and use color-blind-safe colors. Every figure in the vignettes and articles carries alternative text.

    Verification

    • Added reference-parity tests against the original Python implementation (tests/testthat/test-reference-parity.R), covering deterministic kernels (Tier A, ≤ 1e-5) and clustering equivalence (Tier B, AMI).
    • Added tests that drive the server of the comparison app and cover its branding helpers.

    Branding

    • Show the logo in the dimension reduction and visualization color of the package family (deep teal #146554); tools/branding/render.R recolors the approved master artwork and keeps its name outlines.
    • Standardize the package logo across the README, documentation pages and the application header, with matching light and dark artwork.

    Packaging

    • Prepared for CRAN: software names quoted in DESCRIPTION, canonical GitHub URLs, unused Matrix suggestion removed, and the version aligned across DESCRIPTION, inst/CITATION, CITATION.cff, .zenodo.json and the README.

    songR 0.1.0

    Core Features

    • Core SONG algorithm implemented in C++ via RcppArmadillo.
    • Incremental data visualization via update().
    • Projection of new points via predict().
    • Base R plot() and optional ggplot2::autoplot() methods.
    • Supports 2D and 3D output embeddings.
    • print() and summary() methods with codebook and graph statistics.

    Data and Visualization

    • Bundled songR_blobs dataset: 8-cluster, 20D synthetic data (1600 points).
    • Viridis plasma color scale used throughout vignettes and tutorials.
    • All paper figures (Senanayake et al., 2021) reproducible via tutorial scripts.

    Interactive App

    • Interactive Shiny app (run_songR_app()) for comparing SONG, t-SNE, and UMAP side-by-side.
    • Dark mode toggle with localStorage persistence.
    • Upload custom CSV/RDS data or use built-in datasets.
    • Full hyperparameter control, incremental update mode, and export options.

    Vignettes and Tutorials

    • Two CRAN vignettes: “Introduction to songR” and “Getting Started with songR”.
    • pkgdown articles: “Reproducing Paper Figures” and “Interactive Shiny App”.
    • 13 tutorial scripts reproducing all figures and tables from Senanayake et al.
      1. on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, Wong CyTOF (1.27M cells), COIL-20, and Samusik datasets.
    • Extra benchmarks: static AMI comparison, hyperparameter sensitivity sweeps, and runtime scaling analysis.
